overview.overview:
Ohio has moved firmly into the Republican column in presidential politics. The state backed Donald Trump by about eight points in 2020 and by roughly eleven points in 2024, and it now sits about ten points to the right of the nation as a whole. The forecast expects a Republican margin of around six points, reflecting a national environment that leans toward the Democrats but is not enough to overcome Ohio's Republican tilt.

With 17 electoral votes, Ohio is unlikely to be decisive. The chance that it ends up as the tipping-point state is estimated at only about one percent, so campaigns are expected to focus their resources elsewhere.
overview.watch: A substantially stronger-than-expected Democratic national wave, or unusual home-state effects from a Republican ticket featuring Vance or Ramaswamy, could move Ohio's margin noticeably in either direction.
key_factors: Ohio's persistent rightward shift, now roughly ten points more Republican than the nation
A national environment favoring Democrats by nearly five points, which narrows but does not close the gap
Home-state presence of Republicans JD Vance and Vivek Ramaswamy, which could boost Republican turnout and attention
